items.headline: AIRS Medical secures FDA clearance for MRI software
items.summary: AIRS Medical got FDA 510(k) clearance on Oct 5 for SwiftSight Body Composition, AI MRI software that quantifies visceral and subcutaneous fat, abdominal and thigh muscle (including muscle quality and bilateral balance) and liver fat via proton density fat fraction.

items.headline: Health system will use AI instead of radiologists for breast imaging 2nd reads
items.summary: A health system is replacing the human second reader in screening mammography with an AI model — an AI system standing in for a radiologist in a live screening pathway, not an assistive add-on.

items.headline: FDA spells out 2027 AI guidance plans
items.summary: The FDA laid out which AI guidances it plans to issue in 2027 — finalizing rules for AI-enabled devices and drafting its first generative-AI advice — the clearest signal yet on how US regulators will police clinical AI.

items.headline: Utah approves slew of health AI pilots for drug management, women's health
items.summary: Utah expanded its healthcare AI regulatory sandbox with three new pilots that could let AI produce care plans and medications without human review — the first US state to let an algorithm prescribe.

items.headline: AI-assisted telerehabilitation in early Parkinson's disease: a multicenter, randomized, multi-arm comparative trial
items.summary: A multicenter, rater-blinded randomized trial tested an AI-facilitated telerehabilitation system at different intervention durations in early-stage Parkinson's disease, reporting feasibility and exploratory clinical signals.

items.headline: Closing the Automation Gap in HPV-Based Cervical Cancer Screening: Independent External Validation of an AI Model for Dual-Stain Triage
items.summary: An independent external validation of an AI model that reads dual-stain cytology for triage in HPV-based cervical cancer screening — the automation step that screening programs have been missing.

items.headline: FDA clears AI tool for pediatric bone age assessments
items.summary: The FDA cleared an AI tool that performs pediatric bone age assessment from hand radiographs, automating a read that pediatric radiologists do by hand against reference atlases.

items.headline: An open vision-language model for diverse medical applications
items.summary: MedGemma, a collection of open medical vision-language foundation models built on Gemma 3, reports advanced medical image-and-text understanding across multiple imaging domains, exceeding similarly sized generative models.

items.headline: Evaluating large language model responses to unsafe clinical instructions
items.summary: Twenty LLMs were given synthetic cases and records drawn from real clinical recommendations and asked to choose among two harmful and two safe actions, testing whether hospital-deployed models follow instructions that conflict with patient safety.

items.headline: HHS announces new efforts to speed up, expand clinical trials with AI
items.summary: HHS and ARPA-H launched a program to use AI to accelerate and expand US clinical trials, framed explicitly as competition with countries like China.

items.headline: AI outperforms standard methods of predicting organ failure in acute pancreatitis patients
items.summary: An AI model beat standard clinical scores at predicting persistent organ failure in acute pancreatitis, a complication carrying 30-50% mortality — a triage read-out aimed straight at ICU decisions.

items.headline: RFK Jr.'s AI claims spark physician backlash as debate over medical AI intensifies
items.summary: Physicians publicly pushed back after the HHS secretary claimed AI is 'better informed' than human doctors, turning an offhand remark into a fight over liability and where AI sits in the clinical encounter.

items.headline: Insurers say AI could add billions in health costs. Billing companies disagree
items.summary: Insurer studies claim AI-backed provider billing tools are adding billions to US health costs; the vendors answer that the problem is the billing system, not the AI — an early skirmish in payer-vs-provider AI automation.

items.headline: Claude analyzed my genome in 30 minutes. Now we need standards for the results
items.summary: Stanford geneticist Euan Ashley describes an LLM completing in 30 minutes for roughly $5 the whole-genome interpretation that took 30 people nearly a year in 2009, and argues clinical genomics now needs reporting standards.

items.headline: Data privacy concerns could hold patients back from using AI
items.summary: A new survey finds patients increasingly worried about what happens to their health data when AI touches it, a drag on adoption even as AI spreads through everyday life.

items.headline: AI's Healthcare 'Doomsday'? It May Be Less About Autonomy Than Trust
items.summary: An argument that the real risk in clinical AI is not autonomous decision-making but the erosion of trust between patients, clinicians and the systems recommending their care.
